meta.title: beautifulextension — Async Delivery (job queue + alarm drain)

cards.title: The queue is durable, not a timer
items: a job is persisted as {id, type, payload, attempts, nextRunAt, idempotencyKey} — the worker may die at any point and the job survives
one chrome.alarms tick drains the due jobs inside a time budget and re-arms; setInterval dies with the worker, an alarm does not
the drain holds navigator.locks.request("job-drain", …): one drain at a time, even with several worker instances

cards.title: Idempotency is the contract
items: the same job id runs once even if the worker dies mid-flight and the alarm fires again
a non-idempotent call is never retried without an idempotency key
the handler is one use case; long work is enqueued, never awaited inside the event listener

cards.title: Retry classification
items: retryable: network errors, 429 and 5xx — exponential backoff with jitter, honouring Retry-After
terminal: a validation or permission failure — the job goes to the dead-letter store instead of looping
the dead-letter count and the queue depth are visible in the diagnostics export, without tokens or page content

cards.title: What this repo does not have
items: there is no transactional outbox table, no broker and no cron service: MV3 has no server, so the persisted job queue plus the alarm IS the async path
the durable delivery mechanism is chrome.storage plus chrome.alarms, not a Postgres outbox and a worker process
the role keeps its file name for series consistency; the mechanism it documents is the extension one
